note: Each mode is heard against its parent and pinned to its one colour note, shown with the root on a staff; three modes, three keys, three different listening tasks.

exercise.title: Modes by their colour note
exercise.focus: G Mixolydian ♭7 · D Dorian 6 · E Phrygian ♭2, over a drone
exercise.why: A mode is easiest to recognise by the one note that differs from plain major or minor.

sections.text: You do not need to memorise seven scales: each mode is major or minor with one note changed.
Press Play: G major for four bars, then G Mixolydian over the same G chord. Listen for the bar where the sound gets looser.
The note that changed is {{b7}} (F, not F♯). Tap {{1}}, then {{b7}}, then {{1}} again, and hear it lean down to the root.
Press Play: D natural minor, then D Dorian over Dm. The changed note is {{6}} (B, not B♭); it lifts the minor sound.
Tap {{1}} and {{6}} on the staff, then the scale up from {{1}}, stopping on {{6}} each time.

Press Play on the drone on E. Phrygian is natural minor with {{b2}} (F) right above the root: the darkest step there is. Tap {{1}} {{b2}} {{1}} slowly against the drone, then the whole scale up and down, and hear how every phrase wants to fall from {{b2}} back to {{1}}.
